questions.q: With a contact cost of 15, a 30% save rate, and a saved-customer value of 240, what is the break-even precision?
questions.explain: A contacted churner is worth 0.30 x 240 = 72 in expectation, against a cost of 15 per contact. Break-even is where precision x 72 = 15, so precision = 15 / 72, about 20.8%.

questions.q: The base churn rate among active customers is 15.4%. What does the cost model imply about contacting everyone?
options: It loses money, because 15.4% is below the 20.8% break-even precision
It always makes money if the offer is good
It is optimal, since it catches every churner
questions.explain: Contacting everyone has precision equal to the base rate, 15.4%, which is below break-even, so under these illustrative assumptions it loses about 14,454.

questions.q: Why is accuracy left out of the capstone metrics?
options: It cannot be computed for a binary label
It is identical to ROC AUC
Predicting that nobody cancels is about 84.6% accurate while catching no churners
questions.explain: With only 15.4% positives, the majority-class prediction scores high accuracy and has no value. Average precision and precision at k reflect the actual decision.

questions.q: A random scorer on the capstone label gives average precision 0.159, ROC AUC 0.514, and lift 1.00 at k = 369. What is the main use of these numbers?
options: They show the label is broken
They are the target a model should aim for
They prove the harness cannot be trusted
They are the floors: a real model must clearly beat them, and they confirm the evaluation code behaves sensibly
questions.explain: A useless scorer should land near the base rate (AP), 0.5 (AUC), and lift 1. Seeing that confirms the harness works and sets the minimum bar.

questions.q: Why is the ambition target left unset until after the baselines?
options: A target chosen before seeing the data or baselines is a guess
Targets are not allowed in data science
The retention team refuses to set one
questions.explain: Acceptance criteria that can be justified up front (break-even, beating baselines) are fixed early. An ambitious numeric target should be informed by baseline performance.
